items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] That would be -- I mean, wasn't Jack Teagarden and Mildred Bailey, they were both supposed to have been part Indian, weren't they? [INTERVIEWEE] That's true, yes, yes. That's true.

ctx.x: Well, even that, even that. But a lot of people didn't want them to know -- some of them, if they could pass, they didn't want them to know -- want anybody to know they had Indian blood because they figured it would hurt them. You take a real light colored person, a real light -- I've seen a lot of them -- they had -- could pass, and they could pass, they didn't want nobody to know.
That would be -- I mean, wasn't Jack Teagarden and Mildred Bailey, they were both supposed to have been part Indian, weren't they?
That's true, yes, yes. That's true. And this other girl that sang the blues -- I'm trying to think of what her name was. Of course, she admitted hers.
